summary: This document defines a YANG data model to manage OSPF extensions for Segment Routing over the MPLS data plane. Operators can use it to configure and monitor those features in a vendor-neutral way.

eli5.summary: This is a standard settings form for managing OSPF segment routing, so the same tools work on many routers.

questions: what is the ospf segment routing yang model
how to enable segment routing in ospf
subtitle: A standard YANG data model for configuring and monitoring OSPF Segment Routing over MPLS.

tldr.problem: OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 have Segment Routing extensions for MPLS, but there was no standard YANG model to configure them or to read their state.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-ospf-sr-mpls module augments the OSPF model from RFC 9129 and reuses the base Segment Routing model from RFC 9020. It adds instance, area and interface settings, TI-LFA, and read-only views of SR data in OSPF LSAs.
tldr.outcome: Operators get one vendor-neutral model for both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 SR-MPLS. It is a Proposed Standard published in December 2025.

today: RFC 9903 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2025. The metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Module Covers
sections.content:
RFC 9903 defines a YANG data model to manage the OSPFv2 extensions for Segment Routing (RFC 8665) and the OSPFv3 extensions (RFC 8666) over the MPLS data plane. It is an augmentation of the OSPF YANG data model in RFC 9129.

The document uses the RFC 2119 key words as described in BCP 14, and the tree diagram notation of RFC 8340.
sections.eli5: OSPF is how some routers learn the map of a network. This document adds a standard set of settings for the part of OSPF that lets routers steer traffic along chosen paths.

sections.title: Design of the Module
sections.content:
There is one module, ietf-ospf-sr-mpls, covering both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3. It requires the base Segment Routing module from RFC 9020 and the OSPF base model from RFC 9129. It also imports the OSPFv3 extended LSA model from RFC 9587.

The module defines the data nodes that configure OSPF SR-MPLS and the additions to OSPF Link State Advertisements (LSAs) that carry SR information.
sections.eli5: The form clips onto two existing forms, one for general segment routing and one for OSPF. A single new page handles both versions of OSPF.

sections.title: Configuration at Three Levels
sections.content:
Configuration is split by where it applies:

  • Instance: settings imported from the ietf-segment-routing-mpls module, including mapping server bindings and the per-protocol Segment Routing Global Block (SRGB).
  • Area: a segment-routing container whose presence enables SR-MPLS on all interfaces of the area and the advertisement of the LSAs and TLVs that support it. It is only valid when SR is enabled at the instance level.
  • Interface: Adjacency Segment Identifiers (Adj-SIDs) for specific neighbors on multi-access interfaces (broadcast or non-broadcast multi-access). Each such Adj-SID needs a neighbor-id, which is the neighbor's Router ID, IPv4 address or IPv6 address.

An interface-level ti-lfa container configures TI-LFA with the MPLS data plane, as described in RFC 9855.
sections.eli5: You can set things for the whole router, for one neighborhood of the network, or for one cable. Each level has its own boxes in the form.

sections.title: Fast Reroute with TI-LFA
sections.content:
The ti-lfa container has an enabled leaf that defaults to false. Optional tie-breakers choose between candidate backup paths: node-protection prefers a path that provides node protection, and srlg-disjoint prefers a path that is disjoint from the primary path for Shared Risk Link Group links. Each has a priority that defaults to 128, the middle of the range, and a lower value is more preferred.

For Remote LFA, the use-segment-routing-path leaf (default false) forces an SR path instead of an LDP path. It takes effect only when remote-lfa is enabled.
sections.eli5: A router can plan a backup route in advance in case a link breaks. These settings turn that on and say which kind of backup to prefer.

sections.title: Read-Only Views of OSPF SR Data
sections.content:
The module also adds read-only operational state for the SR data carried in OSPF LSAs. For OSPFv2 these are Extended Prefix Range TLVs and Prefix-SID sub-TLVs in the OSPF Extended Prefix Opaque LSA (RFC 7684), and the SR-Algorithm, SID/Label Range, SR Local Block and SRMS Preference TLVs in the Router Information Opaque LSA (RFC 7770).

For OSPFv3 it covers Extended Prefix Range TLVs and Prefix-SID sub-TLVs in the extended LSAs of RFC 8362, Adj-SID and LAN Adj-SID sub-TLVs in the Router-Link TLV, and the same range, local block and SRMS TLVs in the Router Information LSA.

Flag identities such as no-PHP, mapping server, explicit-NULL, value/index and local are defined for the Prefix-SID sub-TLVs.
sections.eli5: As well as settings, the form has read-only boxes that show what other routers have announced, like a noticeboard of labels and paths.

sections.title: A Configuration Example
sections.content: Appendix A shows the same example in XML and JSON. A router with ID 1.1.1.1 runs OSPFv2 with SR enabled. Area 0.0.0.0 has SR enabled, interface eth0 has an Adj-SID value of 3888, and the protocol SRGB runs from a lower bound of 4000 to an upper bound of 5000. Appendix B gives the full tree.
sections.eli5: The example fills in the form for one router: turn segment routing on, give one cable a special label, and pick a range of labels to use.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Access should go through secure management protocols such as NETCONF and RESTCONF with mutual authentication, with NACM (RFC 8341) restricting what each user may do.

The writable nodes the document calls out include the segment-routing enabled leaf, the local bindings, protocol-srgb, the interface Adj-SIDs and the ti-lfa setting. Misuse could cause denial of service. For example, shrinking the SRGB to a very small size could stop many existing segments from being installed, and changing an Adj-SID could redirect traffic.

Reading the LSDB data can also be harmful: knowing the advertised Prefix and Adjacency SIDs could help target the data plane, may reveal the SR network topology, which may be a proprietary asset, and knowing the SID/Label Range, SR Local Block and SRMS TLVs could help attack the advertising node's SR functions.
sections.eli5: These settings steer a whole network, so only trusted people should change them. Even peeking at them could help a bad guy plan an attack.
